snp2.2:0.2: According to the commentary (SnA), this poem is a dialogue between a brahman ascetic, Tissa, and the previous Buddha, Kassapa, who—unlike Gotama—was born into the brahman caste.
snp2.2:5.3: On the term rendered ‘discordant’ (visama), see the corresponding note at Sn 1:12.
snp2.2:11.1: According to the commentary (SnA), this means abstaining from fish & meat.
snp2.2:13.4: Durannaya, here rendered ‘indomitable.’ Notice that being indomitable, a ‘raw stench’ in a discordant person, becomes a positive trait in the awakened one. This sort of contrast provides the basis for the wordplay that the Sutta Nipāta occasionally uses to describe the awakened in a paradoxical way. See, for instance, the conclusion to Sn 4:13.
